correctness.rationale: For the unnormalized rate-one combinatorial Laplacian of a complete multipartite graph with r>=3 nonempty parts, N vertices and maximum part m, spectral projectors give within-part exponent a_i=exp(-(N-n_i)t) and inter-part exponent c=exp(-Nt). For a distinct-part pair the full signed heat-row difference has support in the two parts. The unit-Lipschitz potentials and explicit one/two-cost matching transports prove its W1 cost equals max(f_i,f_j), with f_i=2(1-1/n_i)a_i-(1-2/n_i)c; a same-part Dirac ratio is a_i and cannot beat f_i for n_i>=2. Dirac pairs induce the full measure W1 norm. f_z is nondecreasing in real part size z, hence C(t)=f_m. Differentiation proves the exact formula C(t)=2(m-1)/m exp(-(N-m)t)-(m-2)/m exp(-Nt), the initial curvature N+2-2m, and iff condition 2m<=N+2 for all-time nonexpansivity; otherwise unique global positive-time maximum at the supplied t*. Boundary m=1 (complete graph), m=2, and t=0 are consistent. An independent matrix-exponential/linear-program verification optimized every Dirac-pair transport for five different partitions and three strictly positive times each; numerical finite checks corroborate but do not prove the all-time formula.
